title: Understanding User Behaviour in Inclusive Public Open Spaces: A User-Centric Design Perspective in an Indian Medium-Sized Town
content: Creating inclusive designs is a humanitarian endeavour that unites the lives of all community members to form a cohesive whole while also fostering improved health and well-being. Understanding that everyone utilizes the same location makes it more desirable and helps everyone to focus and participate in the activity. Building codes exist in many locations, however they are typically not readily apparent. Instead, then requiring later changes for those who require specific accommodations, the universal design approach would ensure that all of the restrooms, kitchens, and common areas are accessible from the original drawings. The study looked at the factors influencing how people use public spaces in medium-sized towns in Rajasthan and discovered some crucial data. The results of the examination of public open spaces (POS) in medium-sized towns in Rajasthan show significant variations in the perceived utility according to factors including physical mobility, social group, frequency of visits, proximity, and mode of transportation. Users' impressions of usability and accessibility are also influenced by their physical mobility and method of transportation. For improved accessibility and usability, our findings highlight the need of spatial planning that takes user proximity and mobility requirements into account.
